proposal.title: Aurelia vendor variants — speech music
proposal.reason: Apply the author's vendor-owned/vendor-sold cooperation model and inclusive midpoint >=70% rule. Probabilities are subjective scenario judgments, not historical observations or shipment guarantees. Logix provides design help and AION may supply chips; no OEM-only supply to Logix, Logix ownership or Logix resale is assumed. Preserve historical records and add linked, separately dated scenario offerings. ALF synthesizer — Aurelia-compatible variant: 70–85%, midpoint 77.5%, estimated release 1980-09. Computalker CT-1 — Aurelia-compatible package: 75–90%, midpoint 82.5%, estimated release 1980-08. Mountain SuperTalker — Aurelia-compatible variant: 70–85%, midpoint 77.5%, estimated release 1980-11. Solid State Music SB1 — Aurelia-compatible synthesizer: 65–80%, midpoint 72.5%, estimated release 1980-10. Newtech Model 68 — Aurelia-compatible sound/Morse unit: 65–80%, midpoint 72.5%, estimated release 1980-10. Full reassessment and release basis: data_storytelling/review_evidence/aurelia-vendor-variants/assessment.json and offerings.json.

specification.description: Alternative-history Aurelia offering derived from {source_1}. {vendor} owns, manufactures, brands, sells and supports the finished product. Logix may assist with design and AION Labs may supply necessary chips and ROMs; neither becomes the finished-product owner or seller. The direct release date is an estimated scenario month, not a historical release claim. Existing source products keep their original identities and interfaces.

ALF sells an external three-voice synthesizer with local sequencing/control and Aurelia music software. Commands are buffered and scheduled locally; adding voices does not depend on installing Apple II cards in Aurelia.

The vendor implements FlexiBUS discovery, differential serial transport, framing, bounded requests/retries and flow control using Logix design assistance and AION-supplied interface components where needed. One device connects to each host port; this product supplies no implicit hub or daisy chain. Attach only while the port is quiescent. The peripheral has its own power supply unless the qualified keyboard power budget applies. Vendor-supplied Aurelia Z80/CP/M software handles this device; no arbitrary firmware auto-execution, cross-CPU binary compatibility or later networking/pointer support is implied.

The offering uses the published FlexiBUS transport with a documented vendor-specific device protocol and vendor-supplied Aurelia driver. The scenario schedules protocol definition, device metadata, bounded commands, cancellation/error handling and host qualification before the estimated release. This is not a claim that a universal synth class already existed in the 1978 standard, nor does it add one to the core standard through this product record.

impacted_standards.assumption_description: Alternative-history assessment at the estimated release month of this vendor-owned and vendor-sold Aurelia offering. The scenario assumes the described implementation and host integration are delivered; the date is not historical shipment evidence.
impacted_standards.comparison_description: Implements the FlexiBUS transport; the specialist function uses its own documented vendor protocol and qualified Aurelia driver. No universal core device-class extension is asserted.
impacted_standards.outcomes_description: Adds a vendor-owned Aurelia peripheral path and increases the usefulness of FlexiBUS. This does not imply Logix ownership, exclusive distribution or a measured sales multiplier.
